expectations.text: Frames it as an ITGC deficiency to evaluate through what it undermines: superuser write access to financial data/configurations for ~7 months spanning interim periods
expectations.evidence: "this is an access-control ITGC failure with no direct misstatement itself — you evaluate it through what it undermines"; "six-plus months (February through Q3, spanning at least one quarter-end)"

expectations.text: Applies the severity ladder with correct definitions (AS 2201 Appendix A / Reg S-X 1-02(a)(4)): deficiency → significant deficiency (merits oversight attention) → material weakness (reasonable possibility of material misstatement not prevented/detected)
expectations.evidence: "classification memo with AS 2201 Appendix A / Reg S-X Rule 1-02(a)(4) citations"; MW = "reasonable possibility of a material misstatement not being prevented or detected timely"; ladder applied deficiency→SD→MW

expectations.text: Evaluates likelihood and magnitude properly: was the account USED (activity/log review), what could superuser access misstate (magnitude potentially unbounded), gross exposure before compensating controls
expectations.evidence: "activity log review covering the entire exposure window... whether the account was actually used"; "magnitude as maximum potential misstatement, gross exposure"; "unbounded exposure to every significant account"

expectations.text: Tests compensating controls at precision before crediting them, and considers AGGREGATION with other access deficiencies on the same systems/assertions
expectations.evidence: "test this control's actual precision, don't just note its existence"; "how many other terminated-user exceptions... would aggregate across the population and push severity up"

expectations.text: Leans toward material-weakness territory if the account was usable with no monitoring — and covers the response: immediate revocation, activity forensics, root cause in the termination process, remediation with re-test window, audit-committee communication
expectations.evidence: "matches the canonical material weakness example"; response covers activity forensics, root-cause of "the deprovisioning process break", remediation plan, and "route it to the audit committee"
